about.title: 🏔️ About us
about.text1: CerviniaLive is an unofficial site built by skiers, for skiers. It updates itself from Cervinia's official websites several times a day.
about.text2: The site has no official connection to Cervino Ski Paradise or any other official body. The data is shown as a service to the community.

faq.a: The data updates itself every hour. Try refreshing the page.
Tap “Sign in” in the top corner and choose “Join”.

faq.q: What do the numbers in the banner mean?
faq.a:
The big number is the whole ski area — Cervinia, Valtournenche, Chamois, Torgnon and Zermatt together — the same figure the official website shows. The small number in brackets, when there is one, is Cervinia alone. When there is no separate Cervinia figure, there are no brackets.

The number after the slash is not the total number of lifts, but how many of them are running in the current period. In October, for example, five lifts run in Cervinia and 15 in the whole area; at the height of winter these numbers are several times larger. This is exactly what the operator itself publishes.

The crossing between the Cervinia ski area and Zermatt (Switzerland) over the glacier. The cable car (Matterhorn Alpine Crossing) runs all year in good weather, even when no slope is open — then it says “Cable car only”. Crossing on skis is possible only when slopes are open.

modals.kosher_notice: The food at the huts is not kosher, and we publish no recommendations about food. You can still sit in the huts and on the terraces overlooking the wonderful view, enjoy the winter sun, and have a beer, a soft drink or something stronger — and every hut has toilets for skiers.

swiss.title: Before you cross to Zermatt 🇨🇭
swiss.sub: 200 of the 360 km are on the Swiss side
swiss.intro: The Swiss side is open all year and holds the highest slopes in the area. The crossing itself is easy — but it is bound to one hour you must not miss.

notes.text: ⚠️ **Miss it — at your own risk.** The company's terms say explicitly that there is no refund and no compensation, and that getting back by other means, or a night there, is at the skier's expense.
🚕 The way back by road is 3.5–5 hours and hundreds of euros, and ends in Täsch — Zermatt itself is closed to cars.

🛂 **Passport.** The company's terms require a valid travel document for everyone who goes up to Plateau Rosa and into Swiss territory. There is no fixed border control on the mountain, but it is a binding condition.

🎟️ An international ski pass from the Italian side — €88 a day (against €64 for Cervinia-Valtournenche alone). Multi-day pass holders can buy a Zermatt day supplement at the ticket office — €52 for an adult, €26 for a Junior. From the Swiss side an international day ticket from CHF 104, but the price there is dynamic: that floor is available only 01/11–27/11/2026 and 19/04–02/05/2027, and at the height of the season it is higher.
🚡 The Plateau Rosa/Testa Grigia and Trockener Steg lifts run **uphill only**. You cannot ride them back down.
💳 The currency is the Swiss franc. Credit cards are accepted almost everywhere. Euros are usually accepted — but at a rate the business sets, and change comes back in francs.

💶 Switzerland is much dearer beyond the ski pass too

🥤 Cola 0.33 l€2.71€4.77×1.8

🛃 Customs: into Switzerland up to CHF 150 per person per day — going over means tax on the whole amount, not just the excess. Back into Italy overland — up to €300 per person, and up to €150 for a child under 15 (arriving by air or sea — €430). Cash from €10,000 — must be declared.
📅 The Matterhorn Alpine Crossing — the lift crossing without skis — is closed for maintenance between 07/01/2027 and 26/02/2027. The crossing on skis via Plateau Rosa is not affected.

🏔️ At the start of the season the window is especially short: the last lift up at 14:50, and the Sunnegga-Rothorn and Gornergrat areas open only on 28/11/2026. Until then all the skiing is in the high glacier area — exactly the one most exposed to wind.

why_cervinia.title: ⛷️ Why Cervinia?

items.title: The highest ski area in the Alps
items.text: About 160 km of slopes on the Italian side, and **360 km** together with Swiss Zermatt — one area, one ski pass. The top reaches almost 3,900 m, with reliable snow all season.

items.title: Snow that does not depend on luck
items.text: The high skiing here sits on the Theodul Glacier on the Swiss side, reached through Plateau Rosà (3,480 m) — the highest and largest summer ski area in Europe, about 25 km of slopes. In practice the season opens as early as October, while most of the Alps are still green.

items.title: The Zermatt link
items.text: When conditions allow, the crossing to Swiss Zermatt is open. Ski from Plateau Rosa into Italy and Switzerland and back — in a single day.

items.title: A mountain made for learning and for clocking up kilometres
items.text: Of the 73 slopes on the Italian side only **9 are black** — the rest are blue and red, wide and open. Those still learning, and those who want to cover distance without pressure, get a whole mountain to themselves.

items.title: A quiet, authentic village
items.text: A small village without bustle, crowds or noise. A real Italian atmosphere — whoever is after quiet and a view will find exactly that here.

items.title: Airport and ski-pass prices
items.text: Milan's airports are well served and flights there are relatively cheap. An adult day pass is €64, against about €89 in the Dolomiti Superski and CHF 104 in Zermatt. What you buy on the spot costs less too: in the village and on the mountain prices are much lower than on the Swiss side.

items.title: The Matterhorn — two faces of an icon
items.text: From the Italian side — a perfect, spectacular pyramid. From the Swiss side — the steep peak on the Toblerone. Two completely different views of the same legendary mountain, in one day of skiing.

lessons.instructors_note:
An independent instructor or a school — two different ways:
👤 Independent instructor: you choose exactly who you want, and they set their own price. There is no written contract, so agree in advance and in writing: the price, how and when you pay, what happens if you cancel, and what happens if the lesson falls through because of weather or closed lifts.
🏫 School: the terms are written out in detail — a refund up to 72 hours ahead with proof of the circumstances, and you can add cancellation insurance (Snowcare) for about 7% of the lesson price. On the other hand, the instructor is assigned to you rather than chosen by you; the great majority are excellent, but the personal fit is a matter of luck.

lodging_guide.title: 🏘️ Where to stay in Cervinia
lodging_guide.intro: The village is small, but where you stay makes itself felt every morning — walking in ski boots, parking, and the way home at the end of the day. Here: the village's three areas, what lies outside it, the types of lodging, and what to check before you book.

groups.title: Three areas in the village
groups.lead: On the points-of-interest map each area has its own colour — blue, red and orange.

notes.text:
🔵 Village centre (Breuil, 2,050 m) — between the two lifts that leave the village: the Cretaz cable car and the gondola to Plan Maison. Most of the hotels, shops and the bus stop are here, all within walking distance.
👎 It is also the most expensive lodging, and most apartments are small — sometimes really cramped, with extra beds in every corner. The main streets are a ZTL (Zona a Traffico Limitato — limited traffic zone), closed to unauthorised cars, and not every place has parking.

🔴 Giomein — on the slope above the village, on the gondola side. Quiet, with hotels along Via Giomein — for example White Angel and Bergman Mountain Hotel, right by slope 3BIS. With enough snow you can ski here from slope 3, and down towards the gondola along the line of slope 3BIS (Fallinière) — only in suitable snow conditions. The way down from the neighbourhood and into it is not an official slope and is not on the maps.
👎 The walk up from the centre is steep, and there are hardly any shops. Worth asking whether the hotel drives its guests.

🟠 Cielo Alto (about 2,100 m) — a separate neighbourhood, mostly apartment buildings. This is usually where the cheapest lodging is, and apartments are often roomier for the same price — which is already a treat. You ski from it down to the village on slope 16 (red) and come back to it from the mountain on skis on slope 13, from the Ventina. The neighbourhood has a chairlift of its own, an old one (built in 1972), but it leads only to two black slopes (21 and 22), not to the rest of the lift network. From the upper black (21) the new slope 34 (red, with a steep stretch) branches off to the village.
👎 Far from the village: about 20 minutes on foot up a steep hill, or by car, or on the Linea Viola bus — which runs at limited hours, so photograph the timetable at the nearest stop. The neighbourhood itself has an equipment rental shop. The buildings themselves are very dated and in need of renovation — they date from when the neighbourhood was built, around the 1970s, and some apartments have hardly changed since. Ask for recent photos.

⛷️ True Ski in/Ski out hardly exists in Cervinia. Even "next to the slope" usually means a few minutes' walk. The exceptions: Hotel Lo Stambecco at Plan Maison (see below), and Hotel Baita Cretaz — a small hotel, 7 rooms, on the slope along the Cretaz cable car above the village; for the trip to the village in the evening it has a snowmobile.

links.label: 🎥 "Where to stay" — in the Why Cervinia video

notes.text:
🚡 Plan Maison (about 2,550 m) — one hotel on the mountain: Hotel Lo Stambecco, right at the lift station and on the slope. No road leads to it — only the lift.
More about the hotelThe lift runs 8:30–16:30 and is free for hotel guests; outside those hours — a private snowmobile transfer on booking, so plan your arrival time. The hotel has a gym, billiards and a reading room, and sells ski passes and rents equipment. At Hanukkah it hosts the kosher holiday group of Fun Fit Family — see the Kosher and Shabbat card.

🏘️ Valtournenche — a village down the valley, on the same lift network and the same ski pass. Lodging here is much cheaper. On the other hand, the way to Cervinia on skis is long, and the way up the mountain from the village is by an old, awkward gondola, half standing, and the first chairlift you meet after it, along slope 4, is truly ancient. Be careful not to fall when getting off it. The season here also opens later. And there is an advantage: on a day of strong wind, when Cervinia's high lifts are closed, lower Valtournenche can sometimes still be skied.

🚗 The villages further down the valley — cheaper still. Up to about half an hour's drive each way — reasonable in return for a cheaper, more comfortable apartment. In snow, also allow for snow chains.
🅿️ In an apartment far from the lifts — check in advance where to park, both by the apartment and by the lifts.

groups.title: Types of lodging
groups.lead: The village's official map divides lodging like this — and these are also the terms to search for on Italian sites:

notes.text: 🏨 Hotel (Hotel) — from one star to five. Many offer half board, some have a spa, and some drive guests to the lifts. There are also bed-and-breakfast-only hotels (camera e colazione).
🛏️ Rooms to let (Affittacamere) — a few rooms in a house, usually with breakfast. Simple, and relatively cheap.
🏢 Residence (Residence) — apartments with a kitchen, plus hotel services: reception, cleaning, sometimes a ski room.

🔑 Holiday apartment (Casa vacanze) — a privately owned apartment, through a local agency or online. Most convenient for families and groups, and for anyone keeping kosher — with a kitchen of your own.

groups.title: What to check before you book
groups.lead: "Close to the slope" is not an answer. Ask the place itself:

notes.text: 1. How many minutes' walk to a lift — and which one. Ten minutes in ski boots, skis on your shoulder, makes itself felt every morning.

2. Where the equipment stays. A ski room, a boot locker. If you rent equipment you can leave it at the shop by the lift — the map marks Neloggio Ski Service and SKI 2.0 near Cretaz, and La Genzianella on Via Funivie by the gondola. Then even a place further away is comfortable.
3. Parking. Is there private parking (outdoor or covered)? In Cervinia that is already a lot. In an apartment far from the lifts — check in advance where to park.

4. An apartment inside the ZTL — can you drive in, and how. Some apartments get an entry and parking permit for the whole stay. For others the permit is only for loading and unloading, about half an hour — and the car is parked in the free car park opposite the tourist office. Ask the owner before booking, and give them the car's registration number before you arrive, or a fine follows.

5. How much room there really is. How many bedrooms, and where the "extra" guests sleep. Cervinia has creative solutions: a bed under the ceiling reached by a ladder, beds that fold into the wall, a sofa bed — and sometimes five beds in one room. That is not bad, but when the whole apartment is one room with the kitchen, and at night it fills up with beds — it is less comfortable. Ask for a floor plan or photos of the rooms. In the older buildings, ask about a lift too.
6. What is included. Linen and towels, final cleaning, a washing machine — in apartments these are sometimes extra.

groups.title: Parking — what is marked on the map

notes.text: 🟢 Free parking 1 — on the right, just after the tunnel at the entrance to the village. On some days parking there is forbidden for snow clearing — the days are written on the sign at the entrance. Then move the car to free parking 2.
🟢 Free parking 2 — opposite the tourist office, on Via Circonvallazione, with an electric-car charging point.
🔴 Gondola car park — paid, the closest to the lifts.
🟡 The yellow streets on the map are a ZTL — only permit holders may enter, and there are cameras. Staying inside it? See point 4 above: not every apartment gets a parking permit.

skipass.keycard_note:
🎟️ The hard card (keycard) — three ways to get it
1 · Directly at the staffed ticket office
Buy on the spot. If you have no plastic card, you pay €2 on top of the ski-pass price — a €64 ski pass will cost €66. The card stays with you and can be reloaded on later visits.
2 · You already have a keycard — the fastest way
Buy online and type in the number on the back of the card (with the dashes, no spaces). No ticket office and no machine — the ski pass is loaded onto the card and you go straight to the gate.
⚠️ The card number must be typed in during the order. If you finish the purchase without it, the card can no longer be linked to the ski pass — and you will have to go to the ticket office after all.
3 · You have no keycard
You can order online and collect at the automatic machine, or simply go to the machine and issue one there.
Note: the machine issues a single-use card, free — it is valid for the ski pass you bought and is not meant for reloading. If you want a permanent keycard for future reloads — that is at the ticket office, for €2 extra.
🤖 Automatic machines are in four places: Cretaz · the main ticket office in Cervinia · Valtournenche · Torgnon
🛒 To the shop — buy, or load an existing card📄 The official instructions
The same shop serves both purposes — you choose between them at checkout.
The staffed ticket offices are mainly for purchases with special discounts and for collecting a keycard · the pass is not refunded even if you did not get to ski — check the forecast and the lift opening before you buy

discounts: 🏨 First & Last Tracks 2026/27 — 30% off a 4–7 day pass · until 04/12/2026, and again 05/04–02/05/2027 · minimum 4 nights · you must book directly with the hotel — booking through Booking or Expedia does not qualify

🗓️ Buying online — saves the queue at the ticket office, but the price is the same as the price list. Note: the online shop, the automatic machines and the intermediate stations sell the adult rate only — age discounts are given only at the staffed ticket office.
🎟️ Freedom Pass — 8 rides €76, 10 rides €95, 12 rides €114 · Explore Pass — single ride from €13, return from €20 (Cervinia–Plan Maison)

🏔️ A multi-day pass opens other resorts — a 3–5 day pass lets you ski one day at another resort in the Aosta Valley (Torgnon, Chamois, Courmayeur, Pila and more), and a 6–8 day pass — two days. The days are counted from the pass you bought and are not extra. The Buisson–Chamois cable car is never included.

🗺️ Regional ski pass (Valle d'Aosta) — valid at 20 resorts in the valley, and also at La Rosière in France and at Alagna. Sold as a season pass or as 3–14 consecutive days; there is no regional day ticket. A regional season pass also includes up to 6 ski days in the 4 Vallées/Verbier, one day a week.

🚑 Rescue from the slope costs €200 anywhere in the Aosta Valley. Insurance at the ticket office costs €3.50 a day (a child born after 31/10/2018 — €1.50), or €49 for the season. It cannot be added after purchase.

🪪 The pass is personal and not transferable, with no refund and no exchange. From 3 days up, a full name is written on the pass. The "days of your choice" ticket has no group or over-80 discounts. Tickets sold at intermediate stations, at machines and in the online shop — at the adult price only.

🎿 Quota 2500 — €46.00 · five chairlifts (Cretaz, Campetto, Pancheron, Plan Maison, Cielo Alto), the Baby La Vieille lift and the Cervinia–Plan Maison cable car return. No Cime Bianche and no Plateau Rosà.

howmany.title: 🌬️ How many days to buy a pass for?
items: ⛅ The weather here is changeable. A forecast you can rely on reaches at most about 4 days ahead. And for a day when the lifts are closed by wind or storm — there is no refund: the pass cannot be returned or exchanged.

📊 What we saw in the data we collected (20/2–3/5/2026, 73 days): Cervinia itself closed almost completely on one day, and on about four more days only some of the lifts ran. The crossing to Zermatt was closed on 14 days — nearly one day in five — and once for a whole week in a row (25–31/3). These are end-of-season figures; we have not yet measured the heart of winter.

💡 A multi-day pass saves only a little: 6 days cost €338 for an adult, against €64 for a single day — about 12% less. So it is worth buying a pass for the days with a good forecast, and the rest separately. For example a 4-day pass plus two single days — about €25 more than a 6-day pass, but without paying for closed days.
🏔️ When it is stormy in Cervinia, lower Valtournenche — on the same pass — is usually still open. But you have to travel there and back, and not all of its slopes will be open.

🇨🇭 A multi-day international pass is usually not worth it, because you cannot know in advance when the crossing will be open. Two options: either buy a day ticket every morning as needed — local or international. Or buy a Cervinia pass, and on a morning when the crossing is open buy at the ticket office a Zermatt day supplement — €52 for an adult (for multi-day pass holders; valid on the day of purchase only). rental.title: ⛷️ Gear and rental
rental.subtitle: Cervinia has many rental shops, at different levels and prices
rental.price_sub: The prices of Genzianella Sport, the shop by the main lift station, which publishes a full price list for the season. Every shop has its own prices — this one is here to give a real order of magnitude. Poles are included in the ski packages.
tips: The more days you rent, the lower the price per day — six ski days for an adult come to about €29 a day instead of €41.
Booking online in advance is almost always cheaper, and also saves a queue on the first morning.

If you reach the village in the afternoon the day before skiing — go and get fitted then. The first visit is the longest, because boots are fitted and bindings adjusted, and in the morning the shops are especially busy around the lift opening. In the afternoon the staff are free — they are mostly taking equipment back. Most shops can leave your equipment ready for the morning; Genzianella and Cretaz have heated lockers that dry boots and gloves overnight — on booking, and paid separately.
A helmet is compulsory for children under 18 in Italy, and strongly recommended for adults.
Boots can also be rented separately from the skis (€16 a day for an adult, €7 for a child).
Gloves, goggles and thermal socks — better bought on the way from the airport than rented in the village.

Hours: Genzianella and Noleggio Cretaz close at midday, roughly 12:30–14:30. Cervinia Ski Service is open straight through until 18:00, and Ski 2.0 until 19:00. The shop at Plan Maison cannot be reached before the first gondola.

Overnight locker: at Ski 2.0 a heated locker for €8 a day holds the equipment of two adults — skis, boots, poles, helmet and gloves, dry in the morning. Genzianella and Cretaz have heated lockers on booking, with no published price.

transport.title: 🚌 The way to Cervinia
transport.intro: From the airport to the village you can go by hire car, by transfer or by public transport. This is what each costs and how long it takes.
transport.alert: 🚆 The valley railway is closed this season. The Ivrea–Aosta line is closed for electrification works, and Châtillon-Saint-Vincent station — the station closest to Cervinia — is not in service. Replacement buses run between Ivrea and Aosta instead. The Ivrea–Pont-Saint-Martin section reopens in January 2027, and the section to Aosta only after that. This season the simple way is a car or a direct bus, not the train.

groups.title: Buses — direct and local
groups.lead: There is no direct bus from an airport to Cervinia. All the lines reach Châtillon, and from there you take the local line up.

notes.text: 🔵 Linea Blu (line 503) — Châtillon ⇄ Valtournenche ⇄ Breuil-Cervinia, €3.30 each way, an hour's ride. The full timetable is in the card below.
🎫 Tickets: in the #vdatransports app, at the Aosta and Courmayeur ticket offices, at licensed sellers, or in cash from the driver — in small notes.

✈️ From Malpensa — a direct bus to Châtillon, €25, booking compulsory 24 hours ahead. The stop is the Terminal 1 bus area, on floor -1, by the railway station and opposite the Sheraton; follow the Bus signs downwards, not a door number on the arrivals floor. Does not run on Tuesday and Wednesday.
🚍 From Turin — €15 each way, €25 return, booking compulsory, change at Châtillon. The stops are in the city centre (Porta Susa, Porta Nuova), not at the airport.
🚍 From Milan — the stop is Lampugnano on the red metro line (M1), not a main railway station. €15.50 to Châtillon.

🏘️ Within the village — Linea Viola to the Cielo Alto neighbourhood, €1.20, runs all year. Two more lines are free winter shuttles: Linea Azzurra (the ski bus) and Linea Verde to Cime Bianche. The operator publishes no timetable or operating dates for them, and its line page says whether they are running — worth a look there before relying on them.

🚌 From Valtournenche to Cervinia by bus — Linea Blu stops at Valtournenche on the way up, and so you start the ski day in Cervinia. You can also take the Gran Sometta lift and ski to Cervinia, but it is a long way, partly on red slopes.

🔗 The buttons here open the official website of the operator, Arriva — that is the source, and that is where you book the bus from Malpensa. The timetables in the next cards are copied from the official timetable, valid from 10 September 2026.

groups.lead: Four trips a day on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and one on Monday and one on Thursday. No service on Tuesday and Wednesday. The departure time is from Terminal 1; from Terminal 2 five minutes earlier.

groups.lead: Ten trips a day in each direction, every day of the week. The stop in Châtillon is the railway station, and the stop in Cervinia is Breuil Terminal Bus in the village centre.

notes.text: 🗓️ On Sundays and holidays exactly the same trips, with two small differences: the 17:30 departure leaves at 17:40, and the 6:25 from Cervinia arrives at 7:25.

🎒 On school days extra trips run via Torgnon and so take longer. Up at 6:20 (arrives 7:50), and then the 7:00 trip does not run. Down, an extra bus leaves at exactly the same minute as the regular one — 13:05 and 16:15 — but reaches Châtillon at 14:35 and 17:45 instead of 14:05 and 17:15.

⏱️ Most trips take an hour. Three take longer because they make an extra loop: 13:35 and 17:30 up, and 6:25 down — about 65 to 70 minutes. The last bus up leaves at 19:30 and the last down at 20:30; if you land late you will need a transfer.
🎫 €3.30 each way. The timetable is valid from 10 September 2026.

groups.title: Hire car — what to insist on when booking
groups.lead: Three things to settle when you book: insurance that cancels the excess, snow chains, and a petrol car if you can.

notes.text: 🛡️ Excess-waiver insurance — a must, not an extra. Many companies "find" a small scratch here and there on return, and charge hundreds of euros of the excess for it. The best cover is the rental company's own — but it is expensive. The cheapest: as an add-on to your travel insurance. Buying it through the search engine (such as DiscoverCars) is the same or worse, and usually more expensive. From experience: with AIG a claim is easy, and the refund arrives within a few days, with no excess.

⛓️ Snow chains — they are what always works. The law in the valley is satisfied by chains in the car or winter tyres. Chains are usually included at no extra cost during the compulsory period (at Noleggiare in every car; at Italy Car Rent for €10 a day). Make sure they are in the boot, and that the size on the box matches the size on the tyre wall.

❄️ Winter tyres — almost none. Few companies rent cars with winter tyres, and at a hefty price (for example the WT categories at Sicily by Car, or a supplement of up to €22.20 a day at Locauto). If you can — great, but you still need chains: in deep snow and on the steep climb they always work, and winter tyres are not always enough.

🔧 You will fit the chains yourself. Practise once in the hotel car park, or at least watch the fitting videos before the trip — there is a video for every type of chain, and a hire car usually comes with the manual type. Not something to learn in the dark, in the snow, at the side of the road.
🎿 Ski rack — ask for it when you book, at least 24 hours ahead, for a one-off charge for the whole rental. Not every car can take one.

⛽ Fuel: benzina is petrol, gasolio is diesel. Wrong fuel is not covered by the insurance. If you have the choice, take petrol — ordinary diesel freezes on a cold mountain night, and the engine will not start.

🥶 In a diesel car: on the way up fill with gasolio artico (a separate pump, good to -20°C), or before the cold night add antigelo gasolio as the bottle instructs. If the car will no longer start — do not keep cranking; move it somewhere warm and wait. ⚠️ Never pour petrol into a diesel tank.

📞 Noleggiare at Malpensa is outside the airport, in Somma Lombardo. The shuttle is free but comes only once you phone it — and a pick-up after opening hours costs €50.

groups.title: The law in winter, and the road up

notes.text: 📅 15 October to 15 April — in the Aosta Valley winter tyres or chains in the car are compulsory. A month earlier than the rest of Italy. The fine: €87–€344.

🔎 If you did get winter tyres: the M+S mark satisfies the law, but the tyre that really grips in snow is the one carrying the snowflake inside a mountain (3PMSF). Even with it — the chains stay in the boot.

⛰️ On the road up to Cervinia (SR46) the sign decides. The published order applies to the state roads in the valley; up the mountain the instruction is on the sign at the roadside. Chains in the boot settle the question in advance.
🚧 In heavy snow the road closes. The closure is decided by the local avalanche commission, and traffic moves in escorted convoys at set times. Leave a margin before a flight.
📻 Before you go up — live road conditions on the Aosta Valley traffic website, in the ViaVDA app, or by phone on 0165231243.

🚫 ZTL in the village. The centre of Breuil-Cervinia is closed to cars and watched by cameras at four gates. Give the hotel the hire car's registration number before you arrive — the hotel registers it for the dates of your stay. The fines are paid by the renter, not the rental company.

groups.title: By car across the border — Switzerland and France

notes.text:
🌍 Every rental company has its own rule, and France and Switzerland are treated alike.
• Noleggiare — any trip out of Italy, France included, requires buying a service called the Cross Border Card.
• Locauto — allows the whole EU and Switzerland too, at no extra charge, but forbids returning the car outside Italy.
• Sicily by Car — France and Switzerland are on the list of permitted countries. The binding list is the one printed on the first page of the contract, so read it at the desk.
• Italy Car Rent — a Cross-border supplement is bought at the desk at pick-up, and you must declare the trip in advance.
• At any other company — the binding terms are in the rental conditions on the company's website. Check them before you book.
⚠️ Crossing the border without declaring it voids the insurance and the roadside assistance. That holds at all four companies, and it is the clause that surprises people after something has happened.

🛣️ Switzerland — a motorway vignette, CHF 40. Sold electronically by registration number on the via.admin.ch portal, at the official price and with no fees. Driving without one: a CHF 200 fine plus the vignette. In a hire car — ask at the desk whether there is already a vignette, because most of the Italian fleet has none.

🗓️ Watch the year. The 2026 vignette is valid until 31 January 2027. A trip in February, March or April needs the 2027 vignette, on sale from the beginning of December. In a hire car — check the windscreen first, there may already be one.

🚇 The Great St Bernard Pass is closed in winter and opens in June. In the season you go through the tunnel: €33.50 each way, €53.50 return within 30 days. On the Italian side you pay in euros only, on the Swiss side in francs.
📄 Leaving Italy requires the rental company's approval in advance, and usually a fee too. Ask for it to be written into the contract, and make sure the insurance stays valid across the border.
🛞 Switzerland has no legal requirement for winter tyres — but a driver involved in an accident without suitable equipment bears the responsibility, and the insurance may reduce the cover.

🇫🇷 France — no motorway vignette, you pay tolls on the road itself. A Crit'Air sticker is not needed for a private car on the way from Aosta through the Mont Blanc tunnel to Chamonix — the restrictions in the Arve valley apply to lorries; on pollution days the speed limit is lowered.

❄️ In France, 1 November to 31 March — throughout the Haute-Savoie department, Chamonix included, winter tyres marked 3PMSF are compulsory, or chains or snow socks in the car. Note that the dates and the marking are not the same as in Italy.

season.title: 📅 When to go
season.intro: The season runs from 24 October 2026 to 2 May 2027. Valtournenche runs from 28 November to 25 April. Torgnon and Chamois open on three weekends — 28–29 November, 5–8 December and 12–13 December — and every day from 19 December to 29 March. The right question is not only when there is snow, but when there are no queues.

periods.label: 🎄 The Christmas market in Aosta
periods.note: Marché Vert Noël in Piazza Chanoux in Aosta — every day from ten in the morning to eight in the evening, from 21 November to 6 January. On 25 December it opens at 15:00 and on 1 January at 11:00.

periods.label: 🕍 Kosher ski holiday at Hanukkah
periods.note: Fun Fit Family run a kosher holiday in Cervinia on these dates — a hotel with a kosher kitchen, full board and a children's programme. Details in the Kosher card.

periods.label: 🔴 The Immacolata bridge — busy
periods.note: A national holiday on 8 December, which falls on a Tuesday this year, so Monday is a day off too. Four days of peak demand on a resort that is still only partly open.

periods.label: 🏂 The Snowboard Cross World Cup
periods.note: The competition is held in Cervinia itself. Expect crowds and slopes closed for training.

periods.label: 🔴 Christmas and New Year — the peak
periods.note: The Italian school holidays, and both Christmas and New Year's Day fall on a Friday — two long weekends in a row. From here on the whole area is open every day.

periods.label: 🟢 January after the 6th — the first quiet
periods.note: Italian schools go back on 7 January, and the resort empties. All the slopes are open, the base is already built, and the queues are short. One of the two best windows of the season.

periods.label: 🟠 The Sant'Orso fair in Aosta
periods.note: The Aosta Valley's great craft fair, on 30 and 31 January every year. Schools in the region are closed.

periods.label: 🔴 February — the best and the busiest
periods.note: This is the month of the Settimana Bianca, Italy's family ski week. The deepest snow of the season — and the queues too. The regional school holiday is 8–10 February, around Carnival Tuesday.

periods.label: 🟢 Mid-March — the best window
periods.note: March gets more snow than any other month, the base is still deep, the whole area is open, and the Italians are back at work. The best combination of conditions and quiet.

periods.label: 🟠 The Italian Easter holiday
periods.note: Easter falls on 28 March. In addition, Torgnon and Chamois close on 29 March — in the middle of the holiday.

periods.label: 🟢 The last week
periods.note: Valtournenche closes on 25 April, and Cervinia alone carries on until 2 May. A smaller area, but the whole mountain is almost empty.

months.title: November
months.text: High up only. The lifts go up to the glacier, but the slopes on the Italian side depend on snowfall, and Valtournenche is closed until the 28th. Average base 30 cm.

months.title: December
months.text: The area opens gradually and from 19 December everything runs every day. Average base 44 cm. The shortest days of the season — few hours of light, and cold.

months.title: January
months.text: The whole area is open, the base reaches 77 cm on average. After the 6th this is the quiet month.

months.title: February
months.text: The deepest base of the season — 98 cm on average, and the best conditions. It is also the busiest month, without exception.

months.title: March
months.text: The month with the most fresh snow — about 46 cm a week. The base is still 81 cm, and the days are already long and pleasant.

months.title: April
months.text: Spring skiing. Average base 59 cm, strong sun, and the lower slopes turn soft in the afternoon — so better to stay high.

season.footer: The slopes here face west and south-west and get the afternoon sun — an advantage in January, and a reason to ski high in April. Season dates from the official website; snow depths are long-term averages.

valtournenche.title: Valtournenche — the same network, the same ski pass
valtournenche.text: Valtournenche is not a separate resort: it sits on **the same lift network** as Cervinia, and the day ticket is sold as "Cervinia-Valtournenche" — so it is included. The gondola leaves Plan de La Glaea at 1,524 m and reaches Salette at 2,245 m, and from there you carry on into the area shared with Cervinia. The season in Valtournenche: 28/11/2026 to 25/04/2027 — so it opens later than Cervinia, which is open from 24/10.
valtournenche.warn: 🏘️ The run down here ends in the village of **Valtournenche**, not in Cervinia. Make sure lifts are still open to get back, or manage with a bus.

nearby.title: Torgnon and Chamois — separate resorts
nearby.text: Two small, quiet resorts in the valley, good for a family day or a day when the crossing to Zermatt is closed. **There is no lift connection** to Cervinia — each is a separate trip. Chamois is special in that **no road leads to it at all**: you park at Buisson near Antey-Saint-André and ride the cable car, which leaves every half hour from 07:00 — and every quarter hour at busy times. The last ride is at 22:30, so you can stay up there after dark.
nearby.warn:
🎟️ It depends on which ticket you have:
• One or two days — valid only in Cervinia and Valtournenche. Not here.
• 3 to 5 days — allows one day at another resort in the Aosta Valley, and Torgnon and Chamois count as such.
• 6 to 8 days — two such days.
• A season pass Cervinia-Valtournenche-Torgnon-Chamois — no limit.
Note: these days are counted from the pass you bought, they are not extra.
• Otherwise — their own day ticket: Torgnon €30.50 on weekdays, €39.50 on Saturday–Sunday and holidays (half day — morning or afternoon — €24.50 / €33). Chamois about €25 and about €30. Torgnon: official 2026/27 prices. Chamois: still by 2025/26 — the operator has not published new prices.
🚡 The Buisson–Chamois cable car has its own price list — €3.50 a ride, €5.50 return. You pay for it on top of the ski pass.
nearby.season: 📅 Both resorts are open on the weekends of 28–29/11, 5–8/12 and 12–13/12/2026, and then every day from 19/12/2026 to 29/03/2027.

sources.intro:
Most of the data here comes from an official source — the operator's own website, the Aosta Valley regional database, or an official price list or document. The list below is those sources, one by one.
When two sources contradict each other — we chose one. The site shows the figure from the more reliable source, and the other version is noted here in the list.
We say when there is no official source. The source may be personal experience, the experience of skiers and visitors, an article, a forum and the like.

around.title: 🏔️ Things to do nearby
around.sub: Stormy days, afternoons after skiing, and a day without skis
around.intro: Cervinia is a purpose-built ski resort, not a historic village — on a day the lifts are closed there is not much to do in the village itself. But just below, in the Aosta Valley (Valle d'Aosta), there are castles, hot baths, a whole Roman town and a huge fortress. Everything here was checked against official sources, including what is closed in winter.
around.rules_title: 📋 Three rules that save a wasted trip
rules:
🗓️ Monday is the problem. All the castles in the area are closed on Mondays — Fénis · Issogne · Verrès · Sarre · Aymavilles · Saint-Pierre · Castel Savoia · Castello Gamba — and so are Forte di Bard and the MegaMuseo. By contrast, the Roman sites in Aosta are open every day with no weekly closing day.
So: a stormy Monday — go to Aosta.

🚡 Check whether the activity depends on a lift. Four of Cervinia's five snow routes, paragliding, Plateau Rosà and the snow park in Torgnon — all need a lift that may be closed in exactly the weather that sent you looking for an alternative. Every item here is marked if it works without lifts.

❄️ Wind that closes the top does not necessarily close the bottom. The Valtournenche sector reaches only about 2,432 m, against 3,480 m at Plateau Rosà — about a thousand metres lower and close to the tree line. When wind stops the high lifts, Salette and Motta usually keep running. Chamois and Torgnon are low, sheltered sectors too.
Check the official status page, which has a separate tab for each sector, before you go down.

closed: Castello di Introd — closed all winter. The 2026 season is 4 April to 13 September only. It comes up again and again in searches, which makes it the biggest trap on the list.
Castello di Ussel (Châtillon) — summer weekends only, and 45 minutes' walk from the stop as well. Tempting precisely because it is the closest to the village.
Giardino Botanico Alpino Paradisia (Valnontey) — open only 30 May to 13 September.

closed.text: Museo delle Alpi at Forte di Bard — closed for renovation until 22 November 2026. The rest of the fortress is open.

closed: Gouffre des Busserailles — the 104-metre gorge near Valtournenche. Its winter status is not published anywhere, and a wooden walkway in a wet gorge is a likely candidate for closure. Phone before you go.

places.what: The first floor of the Cervino guides' society building in Valtournenche. The history of the Matterhorn guides and their climbs since 1865, with video screens. Small, but the real thing — this society has existed continuously since the year the mountain was climbed.
places.drive: Valtournenche · about 9 km, a quarter of an hour
places.open: Every day, morning and afternoon (09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:30)
places.price: Free entry
places.warn: The address: Via Circonvallazione 2, Valtournenche. Worth a phone call before you go to make sure it is open: <bdi dir="ltr">0166 948169</bdi>

places.he: Natural ice rink in the village
places.what: A natural-ice skating rink in the heart of Cervinia, lit at night. Skate hire on site, a bar and restaurant that run all day, and après-ski with a DJ from 16:00.
places.drive: In the village itself, on foot · Loc. Campetto 3
places.open: Usually November–March, from 11:00 to midnight. Evening skating over Christmas
places.price: Paid — price on direct enquiry
places.warn: The season and hours change from year to year — check before: 347 049 0770 · info@glow4478.com. This is the only number the operator publishes on its website.

places.he: Open ski slope at the village entrance
places.what: An easy loop of about 2 km at 2,050 m, right by the big car park at the entrance to Cervinia, surrounded by the Grandes Murailles ridge with the Matterhorn behind. Natural snow. **No lift needed at all** — you set off from the village on foot.
places.drive: In the village itself, on foot
places.open: All winter, 10:00–16:00
places.price: Day ticket €7, reduced €5

places.what: A circular ciaspole route (walking in snow with snowshoes) of 3.7 km with a 227 m climb, set up by Valtournenche municipality. You start from the hamlet of Losanche or from the cable-car car park.
places.drive: Valtournenche · about 9 km
places.open: All winter
places.warn: This is the only route around Cervinia that does not depend on a lift — so the only one that works exactly on the day the lifts are closed

places.what: About 55 minutes: a quarter of an hour of technical briefing and then 40 minutes' ride on a snow trail with guides. Adults drive a sled of their own with 3–4 dogs according to body weight.
places.drive: In Breuil-Cervinia
places.open: Through the winter season — by advance arrangement
places.price: Price on direct enquiry
places.warn: Book by phone in advance: <bdi dir="ltr">320 887 6002</bdi>
places.kids: Children from 9 and up to 40 kg drive alone with 2 dogs · children 3–8 ride in the guide's sled bag

places.what: A small lake surrounded by centuries-old larches, right on the SR46 below the village. The place of the famous photo with the Matterhorn reflected in the water.
places.drive: About 30 minutes' walk from the village, or a few minutes by car
places.open: All year, free access
places.price: Free
places.warn: ⚠️ The reflection is a summer and autumn thing. In winter the lake is under snow and ice — a short, pretty walk of 45–60 minutes if you are nearby anyway, not a destination in itself. And even in summer the reflection shows only when the peaks are clear of cloud

places.what: The highest village in the Aosta Valley, 1,800 m, and **with no cars at all** — you arrive only on foot or by cable car. Park at Buisson and ride up. At the top there is a small ski area (1,800–2,500 m, about 14–16 km of slopes), snow walks, and the Lago di Lod — reached by a chairlift that runs in winter, or about 40 minutes' walk from the village.
places.drive: Buisson · about 20 km, about half an hour (estimated)
places.open: The cable car runs all year, 07:00–22:30, a departure every half hour
places.price: The cable-car ticket is bought at the Buisson station
places.warn: The attraction is the village itself — small, snowy and car-free — not the view. So it works even in poor visibility. Plan around the half-hourly departures

places.he: Snow tubing and a children's snow park
places.what: In the Chantorné bowl at the top of the cable car from the centre of Torgnon. Snow tubing, snakegliss, zibob and sledges on dedicated slopes, two conveyor lifts, a beginners' area, and a children's area with bouncy slides, trampolines, a carousel and climbing frames.
places.drive: Torgnon · about half an hour
places.open: Through the winter season — the season and hours change from year to year, phone before: <bdi dir="ltr">0166 540212</bdi>
places.price: Entry €13 · some ski and cable-car tickets include it
places.warn: This is the only snow tubing in the valley — there is none in Breuil-Cervinia itself. An approved helmet is compulsory
places.kids: The best place in the area for children who do not ski

places.what: An open-air skating rink in Piazza Frutaz in the centre of Torgnon.
places.drive: Torgnon · about half an hour
places.open: Roughly 7 December to 15 January, perhaps extended
places.price: Entry €10 · minors €5 accompanied by two paying adults

places.he: Municipal sports centre with a pool and sauna
places.what: Valtournenche municipality's sports centre, open to everyone and not just hotel guests: **an indoor pool**, two saunas, a jacuzzi, a hammam, a relaxation room and a solarium. Plus a sports hall, an indoor climbing wall and table tennis.
places.drive: Valtournenche · about 9 km, a quarter of an hour
places.open: Mainly afternoon and evening — the sauna by advance booking
places.price: €16 for the sauna and jacuzzi — **and the price includes the pool too**
places.warn: Hours change by season, and the sauna works by advance booking — phone before: <bdi dir="ltr">0166 92698</bdi>. Hammam for exclusive private use: €16 per person + €10 per group
places.kids: A municipal pool — no published age limit

places.what: An aristocratic villa from the early 20th century in a 5-hectare park, which today is **the region's museum of modern and contemporary art** — more than 150 works in 13 rooms, among them Casorati, De Pisis, Carrà and Guttuso, and sculptures by Manzù and the Pomodoro brothers. Not a medieval castle — a serious art museum on an estate.
places.drive: Châtillon · 27 km, 40–50 minutes — **the cultural site closest to the village, with no motorway at all**
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday. **Closed on Mondays**
places.price: €6 · reduced €4 · free up to 18 · **the park is free**

places.what: A huge barrier fortress of the House of Savoy from the early 19th century, blocking the narrowest point of the valley, built in three blocks one above the other. Inside are **four museums** — the Museo delle Alpi, Le Alpi dei Ragazzi (the children's), Le Prigioni, and the Museo delle Fortificazioni — and changing exhibitions. **You go up in panoramic glass lifts**, with no climbing at all.
places.drive: About 52 km, about an hour and a quarter
places.open: Tuesday–Friday and Saturday–Sunday. **Closed on Mondays.** ✨ **Open every day from 26 December to 6 January**
places.price: €15 · reduced €12 · "All Forte" ticket for all the museums €24 · free up to 18
places.warn: ⚠️ The Museo delle Alpi is closed for renovation from 13 October to 22 November 2026. The other three museums are open
places.kids: Le Alpi dei Ragazzi is a museum built for children

places.he: Roman Aosta — one ticket for five sites
places.what: One combined ticket, **valid for half a year**, giving one entry to each of five sites in Aosta. The four that make it worth buying: **Teatro Romano** (the south façade of the theatre, 22 m high — the city's signature image), **Criptoportico Forense** (a double underground gallery from the time of Augustus, among the best-preserved underground Roman monuments in the world), **MAR – Museo Archeologico Regionale**, and the **Area Megalitica**.
places.drive: Aosta · about 55 km, an hour and ten minutes
places.open: **Open every day, with no weekly closing day** — except the Area Megalitica, which is closed on Mondays
places.price: €10 · reduced €8 · ages 19–25 three euros · free up to 18
places.warn: The Teatro Romano is open to the sky — save it for a clear spell. The underground Criptoportico, by contrast, may be the most sheltered place in the whole area

places.what: One of the most important prehistoric sites in Europe — a whole hectare, discovered in 1969, with finds from the late Neolithic onwards, inside a purpose-built museum of 12,000 m² and more than 2,000 items. You walk on raised walkways about six metres below street level. **The largest covered archaeological site in Europe.**
places.drive: Aosta · about 55 km, an hour and ten minutes
places.open: Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00–18:00. **Closed on Mondays**
places.price: €7 self-guided · guided €12 · **family (2 adults + 2–3 children) €25** · also included in the Aosta archeologica ticket
places.kids: Fully covered, long hours — works well with children

places.what: A dense cluster of towers and crenellated walls with cycles of Gothic frescoes. This is the valley's postcard castle, and the one to send anyone visiting just one castle.
places.drive: About 40 km, about an hour
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday, morning and afternoon. **Closed on Mondays**. Entry by guided tour only
places.price: €10 · reduced €7 · free up to 18 · combined with the MAV crafts museum for €2 more
places.warn: Fénis is one of the two castles where a real queue forms — worth booking ahead. The courtyard and the painted staircase are open to the air, so in a real storm it is less pleasant

places.he: The castle that is all interior
places.what: The refined Renaissance residence of Giorgio di Challant. Plain outside, splendid inside — frescoes and the famous pomegranate fountain in cast iron in the courtyard. The finest interior in the valley, and the natural pairing with Verrès opposite.
places.drive: About 45 km, about an hour
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday. **Closed on Mondays**. Guided tour only
places.price: €10 · reduced €7 · free up to 18

places.he: A fairy-tale castle with a natural history museum
places.what: The silhouette of a fairy-tale castle on a cliff (the four turrets are a 19th-century romantic addition), and inside it **the region's natural science museum**. It reopened at the end of 2022 after renovation.
places.drive: About 65 km, an hour and a quarter
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday, **10:00–18:00 straight through**. Closed on Mondays
places.price: €10 self-guided · guided €15 · **family (2 adults + 2 children over 6) €30** · free up to 18
places.warn: The lift is out of service when there is snow — important for anyone with a pushchair or limited mobility
places.kids: The best option in the area for an outing with children

places.he: The castle that is two buildings at once
places.what: A medieval core of four towers wrapped in an 18th-century Baroque residence, so the façade reads as two different buildings at the same time. Recently restored and reopened.
places.drive: About 67 km, an hour and a quarter
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday, **10:00–18:00 straight through**. Closed on Mondays
places.price: €10 self-guided · guided €15 · **family €30** · free up to 18
places.warn: The long opening window is the most convenient on the list for those who set out late, after a morning on the slopes

places.what: Unusual in the valley: it sits **on flat ground by the main road**, not on a cliff — so with no uphill walk at all. A complex begun in the 12th century with a residential wing from 1420. The gem is the ceiling of the "Sala delle Teste" with its carved heads.
places.drive: About 65 km, an hour and a quarter
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday. Closed on Mondays
places.price: €6 · reduced €4 · free up to 18
places.warn: The flat access makes it the most convenient castle in bad weather. Worth confirming by phone that it is open in winter before you go: <bdi dir="ltr">0165 904689</bdi>

places.what: A single stern block on a cliff above the town of Verrès, built around a square courtyard — the military opposite of Issogne's homeliness.
places.drive: About 43 km, about an hour
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday. Closed on Mondays
places.price: €6 · reduced €4 · free up to 18 — the cheapest of the big three
places.warn: ⚠️ Access is **a 25–30 minute walk uphill**, and the site is not accessible. **Skip it when there is fresh snow**

places.what: The neo-medieval summer residence of Queen Margherita of Savoy, five turrets, beneath Monte Rosa. Photographs exceptionally well in snow.
places.drive: Gressoney-Saint-Jean · about 75 km, **an hour and a half each way**
places.open: Winter: Tuesday–Sunday. Closed on Mondays
places.price: €10 · reduced €7 · free up to 18
places.warn: ⚠️ This is the longest drive on the list — down to the valley and then up a whole second mountain valley. **A full day, not an afternoon.** The path in the park may be icy in winter. It is also one of the two castles where a queue forms — worth booking

places.he: The great baths at the foot of Mont Blanc
places.what: A large thermal spa built around a 19th-century historic bath-house, at the foot of Mont Blanc: **6 outdoor pools, 9 indoor pools, 9 saunas and 13 relaxation rooms**, plus 40 "wellness rituals".
places.drive: About 84 km · **an hour and a half in winter**
places.open: Open all year, with no closing day
places.price: From €58 (5 hours) · full day from €72 · **evening entry from €54, and "under the stars" from €44**
places.warn: ⚠️ Bathrobe, towel and slippers included — **bring a swimsuit**. Over the holidays the hours change, worth checking the website before you set out
places.kids: 🚫 **Children under 14 are not admitted** — nor are pregnant women

places.he: The nearby baths — and with children
places.what: A thermal centre on the Fons Salutis spring. It has a properly medical side (inhalation, clinic), but what interests you is the **Area Benessere**: indoor and outdoor pools at 27–36 degrees with hydro-massage points, a wooden sauna, treatments and a bar. Not as glamorous as Pré-Saint-Didier, but much closer.
places.drive: Saint-Vincent · about 30 km, 40–45 minutes
places.open: Open every day of the year
places.price: 4 hours €49 per adult / €29.50 per child on weekdays · €59/€42 at weekends · **evening entry €39/€25**
places.warn: ⚠️ **Booking in advance is compulsory** — you cannot just turn up and get in. Worth arranging the day before
places.kids: ✅ **Children are admitted from age 10** — this is the child-friendly bath of the two

places.what: One of the largest casinos in Europe — 3,500 m² on two floors, running since 1947, physically joined to the Grand Hotel Billia. Gaming tables and about 400 machines.
places.drive: Saint-Vincent · about 30 km, 40–45 minutes — **in the same town as the baths**
places.open: Every day from 10:00
places.price: **Entry is free**, and so is the south car park
places.warn: Dress code: the ground floor is relaxed, but **the first-floor tables do not admit slippers, sandals, vests, shorts or tracksuits**, and in the Privé room men need long trousers. You cannot walk in straight off the slope in ski clothes
places.kids: 🚫 **18+ only, with ID** to get an entry card

places.what: The nearest proper supermarket to Cervinia, in località Perolle. This is the honest answer to "I just want a big supermarket to shop for the apartment".
places.drive: Châtillon · 28 km, 40–50 minutes
places.open: **Open every day including Sunday, 08:00–20:00**
places.warn: Châtillon also has a weekly market on Mondays, 67 stalls — you can combine the two

places.he: The only sports shop in the valley
places.what: In the Amérique shopping centre on the SS26, a little before Aosta on the way down. This is **the only Decathlon in the whole Aosta Valley**, and the practical answer to "where is there a big sports shop".
places.drive: Quart · about 48 km, about an hour
places.open: **Every day including Sunday, 09:00–20:00**
places.warn: ⚠️ Closed on 25 and 26 December (on 24 December until 19:00)

places.what: The area's biggest store, in Pollein right next to Aosta — a full Carrefour hypermarket, with a small gallery of shops beside it (about 13 units, among them the sports shop Gal Sport). This is where to do a really big shop: food, household goods, electronics and clothing.
places.drive: Pollein · about 57 km, an hour and a quarter — just past Aosta
places.open: **The hypermarket is open every day including Sunday, 07:30–21:00** · the gallery shops — probably not on Sunday
places.warn: The gallery beside the hypermarket is modest — it is not a mall. For fashion shops the destination is Turin

places.what: A long-standing hypermarket of the valley, on Via Paravera in Aosta itself. Its advantage: it is in town, so you can combine a big shop with a walk round the old town and the Roman sites on the same trip.
places.drive: Aosta · about 55 km, an hour and ten minutes
places.open: Opening hours not published — worth checking on the maps before you go

places.what:
The pedestrian shopping quarter of the Roman city, spreading out from Piazza Chanoux: Via de Tillier, Via Croce di Città, Via Aubert, Via Sant'Anselmo, Via Porta Pretoria. The **L'Artisanà** craft shops (wood, soapstone, ironwork, textiles and ceramics with a mark of origin), clothes and jewellery. A promenade of boutiques and cafés among Roman ruins.
**For really big shopping** Aosta is well served — just not in these streets: the **Gros Cidac** hypermarket in town, **Carrefour** in nearby Pollein, and **Decathlon** at Quart a little before it.
places.drive: Aosta · about 55 km, an hour and ten minutes
places.open: Varies from shop to shop — usually morning and afternoon, with a long lunch break
places.warn: ⚠️ **On Sundays the boutiques are probably closed.** Town-centre shops in Italy work roughly 09:00–12:30 and 15:00–19:00, closed on Sunday and sometimes on Monday morning too. On a Sunday — Carrefour and Decathlon are open

places.what: The Christmas market in the centre of Aosta — local food, wine and crafts.
places.drive: Aosta · about 55 km, an hour and ten minutes
places.open: From the end of November to early January, **open every day**
places.warn: This is almost the only Sunday exception in the whole area

places.what:
**Valtournenche — Friday**, about 19 stalls, all year. 9 km below the village, hardly a drive at all — this is the market worth knowing.
**Aosta — Tuesday**, the big town market, spread over five streets (Via Vevey, Piazza Cavalieri di Vittorio Veneto, Via Lucat, Via Mazzini and the former Foro Boario site): clothes, footwear, bedding, household goods and food.
**Châtillon — Monday** · **Saint-Vincent — Thursday** · **Torgnon — Wednesday** (seasonal).
places.drive: From Valtournenche 9 km to Aosta 55 km
places.open: Each market on its day — see above
places.warn: Aosta also hosts the historic Fiera di Sant'Orso craft fair on 30–31 January, held there for more than a thousand years

places.what: A designed outlet village (architect Claudio Silvestrin) north-east of Turin. **Expanded in October 2025 with €55 million to 140+ shops** — Gucci, Armani, Zegna, Cavalli, Michael Kors, Dsquared2, Coach, La Perla, alongside Nike, Adidas, Salomon, Timberland, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Guess and a Ferrari store. Free parking.
places.drive: Settimo Torinese · about 110–130 km, **about two hours each way**
places.open:
**Every day including Sunday, 10:00–20:00**
On a few peak dates there are extended hours (9:00–21:00) — shown on the website under "Aperture straordinarie". Worth checking before you go.
places.warn: ⚠️ **A full day, not an afternoon** — four hours' driving and another three or four there. This is the right outlet from Cervinia. **Serravalle** is the biggest in Italy (230+ brands) but it is about three hours each way — six hours in the car on a winter day with early darkness. **Vicolungo** is the same drive as Turin but with weaker brands

places.he: The rotating cable car to Mont Blanc
places.what: A two-stage cable car with **rotating cabins**: from Pontal d'Entrèves at 1,300 m, via the Pavillon du Mont Fréty at 2,200 m, up to **Punta Helbronner at 3,466 m** — a circular panoramic terrace and the Sky Vertigo glass walkway. At the middle station: a terrace, a restaurant, the Cave Mont Blanc winery, the Hangar 2.173 cable-car museum, and a children's corner.
places.drive: Courmayeur · about 110–120 km, about two hours (estimated)
places.open: Runs through the winter season — check status and hours on the day itself
places.price: The price varies by season — on the operator's website
places.warn: ⚠️ **The whole product is the view.** On a cloudy day it is money paid for white fog, and it is also the longest drive on the list. **Only on a clear day** — and check the Courmayeur webcams before you set out

places.what: A village at about 1,544 m at the gate of the national park. In winter: **about 45 km of marked cross-country ski trails** (Cogne 1,534 m, Lillaz 1,617 m, Valnontey 1,666 m), and a serious ice-climbing area — about 150 frozen waterfalls in Valnontey, Valeille and the Grauson valley.
places.drive: About 80 km, an hour and a half to an hour and three quarters (estimated)
places.open: Cross-country skiing through the winter · **ice-climbing season: 1 December to 31 March**
places.warn: ⚠️ **The Lillaz waterfalls are the season's trap.** In summer it is an easy family walk of under two km. In winter they become an ice-climbing site, and the walking option is **a guided snowshoe tour** — leaving from the Lillaz car park, about 3 hours, equipment included, **from age 12 and up**. It is a long drive on a mountain road — check road conditions before you set out

around.footer: All times are estimates: every trip from Cervinia starts with the same 27 km of hairpins dropping about 1,470 m to Châtillon, and the times published online are optimistic for winter. Add a quarter of an hour to the first leg, and check road and lift conditions before you set out.
